title: [Decision] secrets: should a read of a datasource's definition keep serving `external.credentialsRef` to every reader that can read the definition? (item 3 of #27818, the maintainer's)
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Ruled: 6522945866 · letter B · 2026-10-30T12:39Z
Ruling-ref: 6522945866

Filing gate: ③ maintainer decision split out of a card that is closing (`security`, rule level only).

**From:** #27818 item 3. Triage (6512259730) classed it as a security boundary and raised it with the maintainer directly. PR #27860 closes #27818's items 1 and 2, so this card keeps item 3 open. Rule-level text only; mechanism goes to the maintainer off GitHub.

## The question

Today a read of a datasource's definition through the metadata read doors serves its `external.credentialsRef` to every caller that can read the definition. After #27762 and #27818 a reference can no longer be written through any non-system door unless it is the row's own. Should the read doors still serve it?

- **Option A, keep serving it.** The GET → edit → PUT round trip keeps working unchanged, and the write doors hold the rule.
- **Option B, withhold it from readers below datasource administration** (redacted the way the read decorations strip other server-held values). The save door then treats an omitted key as "keep the stored reference" for those callers.

## Business reason

The reference is a handle to a stored secret. The write doors are now closed, so this is defence in depth: who needs to see it at all?

**Reader:** the maintainer. No seat acts on it until it carries a `Ruled:` line.

**Links:** #27722, #27762, #27818, #27582.
